findings.statement: Inventory latency increased from 180ms to 6200ms at 14:08, approximately 2 minutes before checkout pool exhaustion was logged at 14:10.

evidence_refs: follow_up_input: checkout logged pool exhausted with all 20 connections occupied, then 503 acquisition timeout
findings.statement: Pool exhaustion is the immediate checkout failure mechanism: slow inventory responses caused connections to accumulate and reach the configured max=20 limit.

recommendations: Supply inventory-service logs from 14:08–14:15 to identify what caused the latency spike (queries, errors, resource contention).
Supply inventory-service metrics (CPU, memory, database connection pool, query latency) for the same window.
Confirm whether inventory responses exceeded upstream.timeout_seconds=30 or if connections timed out at a different layer.
Identify inventory service dependencies (database, cache, external services) and check their health/logs at 14:08.
Review checkout connection pool recovery timeline after 14:10 to confirm when latency normalized and pool was released.
summary: Checkout service experienced a 503 acquisition timeout at 14:10 following inventory latency spike at 14:08. Pool exhaustion (all 20 connections occupied) is confirmed as the checkout failure mechanism. Root cause of inventory latency and connection saturation requires upstream inventory-service logs and metrics not yet supplied.
uncertainties: Why inventory latency increased from 180ms to 6200ms at 14:08—no inventory-service logs or error messages supplied.
Whether the 6200ms inventory response time exceeded the upstream.timeout_seconds=30 threshold or caused connections to queue before timeout.
Whether inventory-service was the root cause, or if inventory latency was triggered by a downstream dependency (database, external API, etc.)—no upstream logs supplied.
Whether connection exhaustion was the only factor in the 503 error or if timeout was also breached.
Whether latency or errors persisted after 14:10, and whether the pool recovered—no later metrics or logs supplied.
